title: Boss: the double-charge postmortem
summary: Work the action items of a real-looking postmortem: find the duplicate charges in the log, show how last-writer-wins lost an update, replace it with a counter that merges, and build an idempotency key store that handles retries in flight.

steps.title: The postmortem
body: **Postmortem PM-118: duplicate charges and lost loyalty points (blameless).**
19:58  card provider p99 rises from 300 ms to 9 s
20:01  checkout clients time out at 10 s and retry the payment (no idempotency key)
20:03  first duplicate charge; support tickets start at 20:15
20:40  loyalty service (two regions, last-writer-wins by wall clock) shows points going down
after purchases; region B's clock found 4 s fast
1. Find every order charged more than once from the payments log (for refunds and the report).
2. Show, with a test, how last-writer-wins dropped a newer update when one clock ran fast.
3. Store loyalty points as a G-counter so concurrent increments in both regions merge instead of overwrite.
4. Add idempotency keys to payments, including retries that arrive while the first attempt is still running.
Each task below is one of those items.

steps.title: 1. Which orders were charged twice?
prompt: Payments log lines look like `20:03:14 charge order=81 amount=40`. Other events (`timeout`, `refund`, `retry`)
appear in the same log with the same shape.
Write `List<int> DuplicateCharges(string[] log)`: the order ids with **more than one** `charge` event,
ascending.
hints: The event name is the second word; skip every line that is not `charge`.
Count charges per order in a `Dictionary<int, int>`, then keep the counts above 1 and sort.
template: Dojo.Eq("orders 81 and 95 were charged more than once", new List<int> { 81, 95 }, DuplicateCharges(dojoLog));
Dojo.Eq("a clean log", new List<int>(), DuplicateCharges(new[] { "20:00:00 charge order=1 amount=5", "20:00:01 charge order=2 amount=5" }));
Dojo.Eq("refunds and retries are not charges", new List<int>(), DuplicateCharges(new[] { "20:00:00 charge order=3 amount=5", "20:00:01 refund order=3 amount=5", "20:00:02 retry order=3 amount=5" }));
Dojo.Eq("ascending by id", new List<int> { 2, 10 }, DuplicateCharges(new[] { "a charge order=10 amount=1", "b charge order=2 amount=1", "c charge order=10 amount=1", "d charge order=2 amount=1" }));
Dojo.Eq("an empty log", new List<int>(), DuplicateCharges(new string[0]));

steps.title: 2. Last-writer-wins, and the fast clock
prompt: Write `string Lww(List<(string Value, long Ts, string Node)> writes)`: the value of the write with the highest
timestamp; on a tie, the write from the node whose name is larger (ordinal). Return `""` for no writes.
The last test reproduces the incident: region B's clock is 4 s fast, so B's **older** write beats A's newer one.
LWW is doing exactly what it promises; the promise is the problem.
starter: string Lww(List<(string Value, long Ts, string Node)> writes)
solution: string Lww(List<(string Value, long Ts, string Node)> writes)
hints: Keep the best write so far; replace it when the timestamp is higher, or equal with a larger node name.
`string.CompareOrdinal(a, b) > 0` means a sorts after b.
template: var dojoW = new List<(string Value, long Ts, string Node)> { ("100 points", 1000, "A"), ("140 points", 2000, "A"), ("120 points", 1500, "B") };
Dojo.Eq("the highest timestamp wins", "140 points", Lww(dojoW));
var dojoTie = new List<(string Value, long Ts, string Node)> { ("from A", 5000, "A"), ("from B", 5000, "B") };
Dojo.Eq("a tie goes to the larger node name", "from B", Lww(dojoTie));
Dojo.Eq("tie order does not matter", "from B", Lww(new List<(string Value, long Ts, string Node)> { ("from B", 5000, "B"), ("from A", 5000, "A") }));
Dojo.Eq("no writes", "", Lww(new List<(string Value, long Ts, string Node)>()));
// 20:40:00.000 real time: B writes 200 points, but B's clock says 20:40:04.000.
// 20:40:01.000 real time: A writes 230 points (the newer purchase), A's clock is right.
var dojoSkew = new List<(string Value, long Ts, string Node)> { ("200 points", 73204000, "B"), ("230 points", 73201000, "A") };
Dojo.Eq("with B's clock 4 s fast, the older write wins and 30 points are lost", "200 points", Lww(dojoSkew));

steps.title: 3. Loyalty points as a G-counter
prompt: Replace the overwritten balance with a **G-counter** (grow-only counter, a CRDT): each region counts only its
own increments, and a merge takes the maximum per region, so merges can happen in any order, any number of
times, and still agree.
Write `class GCounter`:
- `GCounter(string replica)`: this replica's name.
- `void Increment(long by)`: add to this replica's own count; `by < 0` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.
- `long Value`: the sum over all replicas.
- `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, long> Counts`: replica -> count.
- `void Merge(GCounter other)`: for every replica, keep the larger of the two counts.
starter: public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, long> Counts => new Dictionary<string, long>();
solution: if (by < 0) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(by), "a G-counter only grows");
hints: Keep a `Dictionary<string, long>`; `Increment` only ever touches this replica's own entry.
`Merge`: for each entry of the other counter, store `Math.Max(mine, theirs)`.
template: Dojo.Eq("each region sees its own increments", 100L, dojoA.Value);
Dojo.Eq("after merging both ways, eu has every increment", 130L, dojoA.Value);
var dojoX = new GCounter("x"); dojoX.Merge(dojoA); dojoX.Merge(dojoB);
var dojoY = new GCounter("y"); dojoY.Merge(dojoB); dojoY.Merge(dojoA);
Dojo.Eq("merge order does not matter (commutative)", dojoX.Value, dojoY.Value);
Dojo.Eq("a merge never lowers a count", 105L, dojoA.Counts["eu"]);

steps.title: 4. Idempotency keys with retries in flight
prompt: In the incident, retries arrived while the first charge was still waiting on the provider. Write
`class IdemKeys`, the store the payments handler calls:
- `string Begin(string key, string requestHash)`:
- unknown key: remember it as **in progress** with this hash and return `"proceed"` (do the work);
- known key with a **different** hash: `"mismatch"` (the handler answers 422);
- known key, same hash, still in progress: `"in-progress"` (409, retry later);
- known key, same hash, completed: `"replay"` (return the stored response).
- `void Complete(string key, int status, string body)`: store the response. Throw `InvalidOperationException`
if the key is not in progress.
- `void Abandon(string key)`: the work failed with a 5xx; forget the key so a retry can proceed. Throw
`InvalidOperationException` if the key is not in progress.
- `(int Status, string Body) Stored(string key)`: the stored response; throw `InvalidOperationException` if the
key is not completed.
starter: public string Begin(string key, string requestHash) => "proceed";
public void Complete(string key, int status, string body) { }
public (int Status, string Body) Stored(string key) => (0, "");
solution: public required string Hash { get; init; }
public string Begin(string key, string requestHash)
entries.TryGetValue(key, out var e) && !e.Done ? e : throw new InvalidOperationException($"{key} is not in progress");
public void Complete(string key, int status, string body)
public (int Status, string Body) Stored(string key) =>
entries.TryGetValue(key, out var e) && e.Done ? (e.Status, e.Body) : throw new InvalidOperationException($"{key} has no stored response");
hints: Store an entry per key with the hash, a done flag and the response.
Check the hash before the done flag: a different request is a mismatch whether or not the first one finished.
`Abandon` removes the entry, so the next `Begin` with that key is treated as new.
template: Dojo.Eq("a retry while the charge is running: in progress", "in-progress", dojoK.Begin("pay-81", "h40"));
Dojo.Eq("a different request with the same key: mismatch", "mismatch", dojoK.Begin("pay-81", "h99"));
Dojo.Eq("a retry after it finished: replay", "replay", dojoK.Begin("pay-81", "h40"));
Dojo.Eq("still a mismatch after completion", "mismatch", dojoK.Begin("pay-81", "h99"));
Dojo.Eq("after a 5xx the key is forgotten, so the retry proceeds", "proceed", dojoK.Begin("pay-95", "h60"));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("no stored response while in progress", () => dojoK.Stored("pay-95"));
